title: Satellite Link Assignment Under Frequency Constraints
prompt:
Write `assign_links(users, satellites)` to connect as many users as you can to satellites. Both inputs map identifiers to three-dimensional coordinates. Treat Earth as a sphere centered at the origin; a user's outward surface normal points from the origin to the user. Return a dictionary mapping each served user to `(satellite_id, frequency)`, where frequency is one of `1, 2, 3, 4`.

Each user may connect to at most one satellite. A satellite must be within 45 degrees of the user's outward normal, measured along the user-to-satellite direction. Each satellite may serve at most 32 users. Two links from the same satellite separated by less than 10 degrees, measured at that satellite, must use different frequencies. Users with no feasible assignment may be omitted.

Assume valid coordinates with no zero-length vectors used in these angle calculations. Aim for high coverage while keeping the program efficient; a globally optimal solution is not required. Explain how you verify that every returned assignment is feasible.
background_note: The original is a 2022 SpaceX Starlink SWE programming OA, not an xAI system-design interview. The 45-degree visibility, 32-user satellite capacity, four frequencies, and 10-degree separation are reported constraints. The original used a 60-second runtime limit and coverage-based grading; this local Python API and small functional tests are practice conventions, not the original six-case grader. The visible tests use small local coverage targets as smoke tests; they are not the original assessment’s grading cutoffs or a guarantee of global optimality.

example.reasoning: Each user can see the satellite directly above it. Different satellites may reuse a frequency.
